text:
Situation: Sanofi-Aventis U.S. LLC posted a discontinuation of enoxaparin sodium injection for the U.S. market on 2026-10-20, stating the decision is not related to product safety or quality concerns. Corvale East holds 87 syringes of the 60 mg/0.6 mL presentation with 10.9 days on hand at 8 per day, and 246 syringes of the 100 mg/mL 0.8 mL presentation with 24.5 days on hand at 10 per day. Corvale General holds 152 syringes of the 100 mg/mL 0.8 mL presentation with 14.5 days on hand at 10.5 per day.

Why (FDA record): FDA's drug shortage list shows enoxaparin sodium is not listed as of 2026-10-21. A label for enoxaparin sodium names Nanjing King-Friend Biochemical Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (FEI 3010625707) as a registered plant for analysis, manufacture, and pack, last inspected with a VAI classification on 2023-11-10. FDA inspection records for that plant show VAI classifications on 2015-05-12, 2018-04-03, and 2023-11-10.

Our position: Current inventory covers approximately 11 to 25 days depending on site and presentation. Sanofi's discontinuation will end future supply from that manufacturer. Alternative manufacturers are not on FDA's shortage list today.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to place orders with Amphastar Pharmaceuticals, Inc. for both presentations; requires P&T committee approval.
2. Buyer to qualify BE Pharmaceuticals Inc., Civica, Inc., Gland Pharma Limited, and Hebei Changshan Biochemical Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. as backup sources; requires P&T committee approval.
3. Buyer to monitor FDA shortage list daily and report changes to P&T committee chair; requires pharmacy director approval.

Not recommended: Delaying procurement until Sanofi inventory is exhausted.
